premises: H1 collision law with epsilon re-derived at the derived longer-entry bound, extended to the small-key adder table (adder logarithms uniform on the accepted set)
M1 and L-ori including conditional fresh-class exposure
H3 instruction pricing and forced-path bounds; fixed path measured at 2^20 walks and 2^20 adders
H-trail: for a trail from fresh coins (table fixed), expected blinded-average metered correction instructions at most CORR per expected processed step (abort probability only)
limitations: Conditional analytic bound; no full-size attack execution.
Rare-path prices, forced maxima and reduced-order evidence originate from the predecessor unless separately identified.

Instruction counts are exact emulated counts (QEMU user mode) of builds made in the organizer's reference-count image, cross-checked against that image's Callgrind on the previous revision's kernel at 2^16 walks; a 1,024-instruction allowance per round covers method and toolchain differences.
The 2^24-adder step is compared with the measured 2^20-adder step by disassembly, not measured.
The anchor round difference is measured at 2^16 walks and carried to 2^20 walks by its exact per-step form.
Correction work is metered and capped; H-trail is an average-only heuristic premise that affects only the abort probability.

This revision's counts use the Ubuntu GCC 14.2.0 cross build and QEMU 8.2.2 outside the organizer image; the new kernel's fixed path equals the previous kernel's in the same toolchain, whose organizer-image count is charged.
Small-key adder effect on the production collision law is supported by toy runs only.
